___

**DEF**)
An [[Integral Domain|integral domain]] $D$ is a **principal ideal domain (PID)** if every [[Ideal|ideal]] in $D$ is a [[Principal ideal|principal ideal]].

___

**EXAMPLE**)

* We know that $\mathbb{Z}$ is PID since every ideal in $\mathbb{Z}$ is of the form $n\mathbb{Z}$, generated by some integer $n$.

* [[Thm 27.24]] says that if $F$ is a [[Field|field]], then $F[x]$ is PID.

___
